passages.t: ‘A song for the Sabbath day’: still bearing fruit in old age
passages.happening:
The heading reads, “A Psalm. A song for the Sabbath day” (verse 1). It is the only psalm whose heading names the Sabbath. It begins, “It is good to praise the LORD, and to sing praises to Your name, O Most High” (verse 1). Morning and night, with harp and lyre, the singer tells of God's loving devotion and faithfulness (verses 2 to 3).

The reason for the joy is what God has done. “For You, O LORD, have made me glad by Your deeds; I sing for joy at the works of Your hands” (verse 4). “How great are Your works, O LORD, how deep are Your thoughts” (verse 5).

The psalm then sets two kinds of growth side by side. The wicked “sprout like grass” for a short time and are gone (verse 7). But the righteous are like trees. “The righteous will flourish like a palm tree, and grow like a cedar in Lebanon” (verse 12). “In old age they will still bear fruit; healthy and green they will remain” (verse 14).

It ends with a confession: “The LORD is upright; He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness” (verse 15).
passages.hearers:
The Sabbath was the seventh day, a day of rest. It remembered that God rested after making the world, “Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy” (Exodus 20:11). It was also a day of worship.

The Mishnah, an early collection of Jewish teaching, lists a psalm that the Levites sang in the temple for each day of the week. Psalm 92 is the psalm for the Sabbath. It is still sung in Jewish Sabbath worship. It never mentions the Sabbath in its verses. But it is full of joy in what God's hands have made, and that fits a day that remembers creation.

The two trees were well chosen. The date palm grows tall and keeps bearing fruit for many years. The cedars of Lebanon were the greatest trees anyone in Israel knew, used for the temple itself. Grass springs up after rain and is gone in a few days. A first hearer would see the difference at once.
passages.later:
Psalm 1 also pictures the righteous as a tree “planted by streams of water” (Psalm 1:3). Jeremiah says the one who trusts the LORD “is like a tree planted by the waters”, whose “leaves are always green” (Jeremiah 17:8).

Jesus said, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath” (Mark 2:27). Hebrews speaks of a rest still to come: “There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God” (Hebrews 4:9).
passages.asks:
Is there a day in your week set apart for rest and praise? Psalm 92 suggests that rest is not only stopping work. It is gladness at what God has done.

And let verse 14 encourage anyone growing old. Age does not mean uselessness in God's house. Older people who are rooted in God can still bear fruit: prayer, wisdom, kindness, a life that tells the young, ‘The LORD is upright.’
